{
  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Flux batch script converted from LSF

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# LSF resources:
#   -J NET-seq
#   -o logs/snake_%J.out
#   -e logs/snake_%J.err

#flux: --job-name=NET-seq

# Omitted LSF options: -o/-e with %J token
# LSF's %J token expansion is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

module load fastqc
module load bowtie2
module load samtools
module load subread
module load gcc/7.4.0
module load R/4.0.3

mkdir -p logs

# Function to run snakemake
run_snakemake() {
    local snake_file=$1
    local config_file=$2

    args='
        -oo {log.out} 
        -eo {log.err} 
        -J {params.job_name}
        -R "rusage[mem={params.memory}] span[hosts=1]"
        -n {threads} '

    # LSF/DRMAA submission is not portable to Flux.
    # Omitted: --drmaa "$args"
    # Performance implication: rules will not be submitted as separate scheduler jobs; they will run within this single allocation,
    # which can reduce throughput unless you configure a Flux-native Snakemake executor/profile.
    snakemake -n \
        --snakefile "$snake_file" \
        --jobs 100 \
        --configfiles $config_file
}

pipe_dir=src/pipelines
samples=SAMPLES.yaml

snake=$pipe_dir/NETseq.snake
config=NETseq.yaml
run_snakemake "$snake" "$samples $config"

snake=$pipe_dir/pauses.snake
config=pauses.yaml
run_snakemake "$snake" "$samples $config"
"
}
